detail.title: Reverse a String
statement: You get a string `s` made of English letters and digits. Return a new string with the same characters in reverse order, so the last character comes first and the first comes last.
Keep every character exactly as it is, including its case.

params.name: s
params.description: the string to reverse

returns.description: the characters of s in reverse order

constraints: `s` contains only English letters (`a` to `z`, `A` to `Z`) and digits (`0` to `9`).

examples.explanation: A single character reads the same both ways.

hints: The first character of the answer is the last character of `s`. Which index is that?
Walk an index from the end of the string back to the start and collect each character.
For the in-place version, put one pointer at each end, swap, and move them towards each other until they meet.

solution.summary: Every character has a fixed destination: the one at index `i` belongs at index `n-1-i`. Write the characters into a new string in that order, or swap them in pairs from both ends. The swap is the version interviewers ask for, because the same two pointer move reverses an array in place and checks a palindrome.

approaches.title: Copy the characters from the back
Swap from both ends with two pointers

intuition: The reverse starts with the last character and ends with the first, so loop an index from `n-1` down to `0` and append each character to the answer.
Append to a list or a string builder and join once at the end. Adding one character to an immutable string with `+` copies the whole string each time.
steps: Create an empty list or string builder for the answer.
Join the answer into a string and return it.
pitfalls: Looping `left` all the way to `n-1`. Past the middle every pair is swapped back and the string comes back unchanged. Stop at `left < right`.
Starting the backward loop at `n` instead of `n-1`, which reads one position past the end.
Swapping without a temporary variable. After `chars[left] = chars[right]` the old left character is gone.

faqs.question: What is the time complexity of reversing a string?
faqs.answer: O(n): every character is read once and written once.

faqs.question: How do you reverse a string without a built-in reverse function?
faqs.answer: Walk two pointers from both ends towards the middle and swap the characters they point at.

faqs.question: Can you reverse a string in place?
faqs.answer: Only if the language lets you change the characters (C++, or a char array in Java). Python and JavaScript strings are immutable, so you build a new one.
